summary:
Sowcast helps smallholder farmers in Southeast Asia decide what to plant next season in a climate that no longer behaves the way it used to. For 31 farming regions in Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Malaysia, it turns 24 years of NASA and open satellite data (NASA POWER weather, CHIRPS rainfall, MODIS and VIIRS greenness, SRTM terrain, SoilGrids soil) into a month-by-month rain calendar, trends projected to 2035 with plain-language consequences, crop rankings, and crop rotations matched to the farmer's goal: soil health, income, saving water or low risk.
Farmers can check their own rotation in a drag-and-drop builder and download a printable plan, translatable in the browser, covering the rotation, each crop, how to grow it and a season checklist. A Claude skill brings the same analysis to any location through chat.

It matters because most smallholders plan from memory and habit while rain, heat and dry spells shift around them. Every number shows its source, and projections are clearly labelled, so farmers and extension workers can trust it, question it and act on it.
details:
What it does. Sowcast is a web app in four steps. (1) Pick a farming region on a map coloured by NASA plant greenness. (2) Read a satellite brief: rain against crop water need month by month, heat days, downpours, dry spells and soil since 2001, satellite images of the area in its barest and greenest months, and a 2035 outlook that turns trends into consequences ("about 30 more scorching days a year; groundnut and pulses most exposed; what to do"). (3) Compare crop rotations: what farmers do now next to the best three for a chosen goal, with a crop calendar and scores, or build your own. (4) Rank 25 crops for your goal and download a printable plan. A Claude skill offers the same advice in chat, for any coordinates.
How it works. A Node and Python pipeline downloads daily data for 2001–2024 and checks its quality. It detects a known 2008 fault in NASA POWER data and swaps in CHIRPS and ERA5 where needed, and corrects temperature for elevation. Trends use Mann-Kendall tests and Theil–Sen slopes, projected to 2035 with an 80% range. Crops are scored with our team's agronomic rules, and a recommender ranks every valid rotation for six goals.
Impact. Better rotations protect soil, cut fertiliser costs and reduce crop failure in bad years.

Tools. React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Recharts, Leaflet, Framer Motion; Python (pandas, SciPy, pymannkendall); Node; Vercel; Claude Code. Creativity and considerations. Every number shows its source, projections are visibly marked, low-confidence data is flagged, the app works on phones, plans can be translated before printing, and Sowy, our seed mascot, makes it friendly.
